question: Parliament’s Abraham Accords Network was created in June 2023 to support diplomatic normalisation between Israel and the Arab world. Hamas’ act of terrorism on 7 October 2023 shattered hopes for durable progress towards peace: Israel’s security situation remains parlous and the people of Gaza continue to face a humanitarian crisis, including a looming famine. Yet hope is not lost.

The September 2020 Abraham Accords Declaration espouses the common values of tolerance, dialogue, respect for human dignity and freedom. A two-state solution remains the best way to achieve peace in a secure, prosperous Middle East. The Abraham Accords are an essential supporting framework towards this goal.

Along with other aid, the Commission has allocated EUR 18 million to strengthen regional stability in support of the Abraham Accords, in particular in light of 7 October. This investment in peace must continue. We therefore ask: 1.

How are the additional funds itemised in the Commission’s November 2023 Action Document for ‘Regional EU-Israel cooperation in support of the Abraham Accords, and fight against antisemitism and fostering Jewish life’ helping to develop a culture of peace throughout the Middle East, particularly regarding education?
How can EU support for the Abraham Accords be made systemic so it contributes to a growing and sustainable Middle East peace process?
answer: The EU has welcomed the normalisation of relations between Israel and several Arab states in the region. The EU is exploring opportunities for regional and trilateral cooperation and joint initiatives opening up new perspective for business, people, trade, travel, research, the environment, as well as in a number of other areas.

The EU reiterates its commitment to a comprehensive and lasting peace for the entire region and stands ready to work to this end together with its regional and international partners. In this regard, the EU will continue to encourage the establishment of diplomatic relations between Israel and Arab countries, also in relation with the Middle East Peace Process (1).

The EU Action ‘Regional EU-Israel cooperation in support of the Abraham Accords, and fight against antisemitism and fostering Jewish life’ (2), aims at building on the EU’s engagement in the region, to explore opportunities for regional and trilateral cooperation, and facilitate and accompany interactions and development of joint initiatives and projects between Israel and countries in the region in support of the Abraham Accords.

The EU funded action seeks also to support the global fight against antisemitism, by contributing to Holocaust remembrance, education and research. In this sense, the action provides support to the Valley of the Communities initiatives of Yad Vashem — the World Holocaust Remembrance Centre — as a testimony of Jewish life in Europe before the Holocaust.

Education and knowledge on the Holocaust will support the fight against antisemitism, in contexts where antisemitic incidents have increased following the attack by Hamas against Israel on 7 October 2023, and the Israel-Hamas war in Gaza.
